question: Andy the Ant lives on a coordinate plane and is currently at \((-20, 20)\) facing east (that is, in the positive \(x\)-direction). Andy moves \(1\) unit and then turns \(90^{\circ}\) left. From there, Andy moves \(2\) units (north) and then turns \(90^{\circ}\) left. He then moves \(3\) units (west) and again turns \(90^{\circ}\) left. Andy continues this process, increasing his distance each time by \(1\) unit and always turning left. What is the location of the point at which Andy makes the \(2020\text{th}\) left turn?
solution:
Four left turns bring Andy back to facing east, so grouping the moves in fours lets us find a repeated coordinate change.

For any integer \(k\geq0\), moves \(4k+1\) through \(4k+4\) go east, north, west, and south, respectively. Their horizontal change is
\[
(4k+1)-(4k+3)=-2,
\]
and their vertical change is
\[
(4k+2)-(4k+4)=-2.
\]
Thus every group of four moves takes Andy \(2\) units west and \(2\) units south, even though the individual moves keep getting longer.

Andy makes his \(2020\)th turn immediately after his \(2020\)th move. Since \(2020=4\cdot505\), his coordinates then are
\[
\begin{aligned}
x&=-20-2(505)=-1030,\\
y&=20-2(505)=-990.
\end{aligned}
\]
The location is \(\boxed{(-1030,-990)}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Andy’s horizontal coordinate depends on his total eastward and westward travel, while his vertical coordinate depends on his total northward and southward travel. We can calculate these four totals separately.

The directions repeat every four moves. Among the first \(2020\) moves there are \(505\) moves in each direction, with distances as follows:

| Direction | Distances | Total distance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| East | \(1,5,9,\ldots,2017\) | \(505(1+2017)/2=509{,}545\) |
| North | \(2,6,10,\ldots,2018\) | \(505(2+2018)/2=510{,}050\) |
| West | \(3,7,11,\ldots,2019\) | \(505(3+2019)/2=510{,}555\) |
| South | \(4,8,12,\ldots,2020\) | \(505(4+2020)/2=511{,}060\) |

Each row is an arithmetic sequence. Pairing its first and last terms, then its second and next-to-last terms, shows that its average is half the sum of its endpoints. Multiplying that average by \(505\) gives the totals in the table.

At the \(2020\)th turn, Andy has finished these \(2020\) moves. His coordinates are therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
x&=-20+509{,}545-510{,}555=-1030,\\
y&=20+510{,}050-511{,}060=-990.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{(-1030,-990)}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
